$comment: A VARIABLY MODIFIED TYPEDEF USED BEFORE A SAME-NAMED ONE DECLARED LATER KEEPS ITS OWN BOUND (C 6.2.1p7, C 6.7.8p3; P69 round 1, lane cs, fold f26c -- a neighbour of D-C-A-NAME-USED-BEFORE-ITS-DECLARATION-BINDS-THE-LATER-ONE, its class-closure sweep). `typedef int R[n]; { R a; typedef int R[m]; R b; }`: `a` has the OUTER typedef (n ints), `b` the inner one (m ints). The type resolver already chose the outer typedef for `a`, in order; the VLA typedef ORIGIN (the typedef whose frozen bound sizes the object) was recovered by a second, order-blind lookup of the alias name, which found the inner typedef declared after `a`. Probe nt cell 8 measures the references (gcc and clang; cl implements no VLA). Every return before 42 names the first fact that failed; the release arm pins that the optimizer reads the same sizes.
